page_title: Amplitude CLI — Author Amplitude Projects From Your Terminal
page_description: The official command-line tool to manage your Amplitude projects: create, author, validate and build, by hand or from a script.
hero_title: Author Amplitude Projects From Your Terminal

wf_title: From Empty Folder To Runtime Assets
wf_lead: Amplitude is data-driven: the SDK reads JSON. The CLI writes, checks and packages that JSON for you.
wf1_body: Scaffold the project folders from a template. The project is registered with the CLI unless you say otherwise.
wf2_body: Sounds, collections, effects, switches, events, soundbanks, attenuations, RTPCs, pipelines and buses, with prompts when you leave a value out.
wf3_body: Check every asset, bus file and engine config against the SDK schemas, references included, or one type at a time while you iterate.
wf4_body: Validate, then write runtime-ready assets to a build folder. Clean it first, or stop at the first error.
cmds_lead: Run `am --help` for the full list, or append `--help` to any command for detailed instructions
note_project: Create and manage projects, then validate and build them.
note_asset: Manage the assets of the current project: am asset <type> <action>. Deleting an asset that is still referenced is refused.
note_config: Mixing and engine setup files in the sources folder of your project.
note_template: A default template ships with the CLI. Register your own from any directory.
note_tools: Check your setup and install tab completion.
cmd_project_init: Create a new project from a registered template.
cmd_project_unregister: Unregister a project, and optionally delete its files.
cmd_project_favorite: Mark or unmark a project as favorite.
cmd_project_info: Show details of a project. Uses the current directory when no name is given.
cmd_project_validate: Validate every asset, bus file and engine config in a project, or only one type.
cmd_project_build: Build project assets for runtime consumption.
cmd_asset_sound: Audio files with gain, bus, priority, looping, streaming, spatialization, attenuation and RTPC-driven values.
cmd_asset_collection: Groups of sounds with a play mode and a scheduler mode.
cmd_asset_effect: An effect type, such as reverb or EQ, with its parameters. Compiled to .amfx on build.
cmd_asset_switch: A named set of states. State IDs are kept across edits.
cmd_asset_switch_container: Maps each state of a switch to a sound.
cmd_asset_event: Triggerable actions, run in parallel or in sequence.
cmd_asset_soundbank: Packages assets for runtime. Include or remove them by type and name.
cmd_asset_attenuation: Distance falloff with a shape, a max distance, inner and outer radii and curve parts.
cmd_asset_rtpc: A real-time parameter with a min, max and default value, to drive sound values from gameplay.
cmd_asset_pipeline: Audio processing node graphs. Refused while an asset or an engine config uses it.
cmd_asset_bus: Buses inside a *.buses.json file. The master bus, buses with children and buses in use stay.
cmd_asset_bus_file: The *.buses.json files themselves. A new file holds only the master bus; the last file stays.
cmd_asset_engine_config: The *.config.json engine configuration files. The last one cannot be deleted.
cmd_template_info: Display detailed information about a template.
cmd_template_register: Register a custom template from a directory.
cmd_sdk_check: Check that the Amplitude SDK is properly configured.
cmd_completions: Generate a shell completion script for commands, subcommands and flags.
scr_title: Friendly By Hand, Predictable In A Script
scr_lead: Leave a value out and the CLI asks for it. Pass `--non-interactive` and it fails instead of prompting.
scr_b1: Machine-readable output with `--json` on any command
scr_b2: Distinct error codes for validation, assets, projects, SDK and build failures
scr_b3: References are strict: a missing asset is an error, and delete refuses an asset that is still in use
scr_b4: Shell completions for bash, zsh and fish
road_title: Early Today, Growing In The Open
road_lead: The CLI is at version 0.1 and changes quickly. A terminal UI is planned next, for browsing and editing a project without leaving the terminal.
road_i1: Project lifecycle: init, register, list, favorite, info
road_i2: Assets lifecycle: create, list, update, delete, with reference checks
road_c2_body: An interactive view of a project, driven by the keyboard, on top of the same commands. This sketch only shows the idea and will change.
road_sketch_aria: Concept sketch of the planned terminal UI: an asset list, an inspector and a validation panel
